purpose: Close weak stable-ID and same-broad-ancestor promotion paths while preserving reproducible evidence.
requirements: Do not treat a non-empty data-offer-id or arbitrary id as stable. Define and enforce an auditable card-scoped identifier schema, or validate it against a sealed metadata mapping; record the proof in output.

Banned page/broad containers (including post-content, entry-content, main and section shells) remain ineligible even when they contain an identifier, unless a structural card marker and card-scoped identifier are both present.

Prove locality binding phrase plus locality target in the same semantic text node, or in a tightly specified sibling relation belonging to the selected card. Prove validity/recurrent claim and target year similarly; container-wide text search is forbidden.

Add a mandatory regression: post-content data-offer-id=x containing an offer title/price, unrelated Hanoi promotion clause, unrelated Da Nang travel text, unrelated 2026 branding text, and recurrence. It must return HELD.

Add attacks for arbitrary data-offer-id, generic id, nested broad shell with a child card, and multiple unrelated semantic paragraphs inside one accepted card. Include a positive control exercising the accepted identifier schema.

Add a non-mutating verify-existing replay mode. It must calculate expected artifacts in memory and fail on any difference from current matrix, test report, receipt or sidecars; generation mode must be explicit and never overwrite sealed evidence by default.
Evaluate only existing R3 vault bytes. Preserve 0 VERIFIED / 10 HELD unless every requirement independently passes. Do not hydrate, package, deploy, mutate scheduler/alias or rollback.
acceptance_gate: CEO verify-existing replay and code review required; no automatic promotion
